Changeling Wayfinder: Solid fixer, not glue. A changeling body that fetches a basic smooths any base and keeps you open to every typal payoff, but the 1/2 doesn't affect the board — Ethan loved it, Ben was cool on it, and the 53.6% WR pegs it as a fine role-player fixer, not a build-around.
Rooftop Percher: Solid role-player that overdelivers on its unexciting body. A five-mana colorless changeling flyer that gains 3 and hits graveyards is generic playable in any deck, and 55% GIH is real — the changeling type and evasion do quiet work. Not a first pick, but always fine.
Adept Watershaper: Premium UW build-around and a fine standalone 3/4 for {2}{W}. Making your tappers indestructible turns convoke/tap synergies into free attacks and blanks combat and Cinder Strike on anything tapped. Near-universal 88% play rate and strong 57.9% GIH WR — snap it in Merfolk, take it early anywhere white.
Ajani, Outland Chaperone: First-pick bomb. A 3-mana walker that either builds a board of Kithkin tokens or fires a repeatable 4-damage removal ping at tapped attackers — and the +8.7 IWD with 60.9% GIH confirms it takes over games regardless of archetype. Slam it P1P1.
Appeal to Eirdu: Filler combat trick. A 50% GIH WR and negative IWD mark a marginal buff spell you play mostly as convoke-fodder in a wide UW/GW board; two-target mode gives it reach but it does nothing to the board and gets sideboarded in most decks. Late-pick synergy piece, not a maindeck default.
Bark of Doran: Sideways build-around, not a maindeck staple: sub-50% GIH WR and negative IWD confirm it's a do-nothing without the right shell. Best in UW merfolk (1/3s swing as 4/4s) or on Reaping Willow. Draft it late as spice, not a priority.
Brigid, Clachan's Heart: First-pickable W rare: a 3/2 that immediately makes a Kithkin token and flips into a repeatable creature-count mana engine. 60.9% GIH, +8.6 IWD and a pick-2 ALSA confirm it overperforms the raw body — the tokens fuel GW/Vivid go-wide. Take it and build W.
Burdened Stoneback: Solid role-player. A 2/2 body for two that grows as it feeds indestructible to your best threat is fine on rate, but the payoff comes in BW blight where the -1/-1 counters are an asset, not a tax. Middling 53% WR reflects a body that needs the deck around it.
Champion of the Clachan: Premium in Kithkin (GW), a hard sell elsewhere. Flash 4/5 that anthems your Kithkin and re-buys the exiled one on death is a genuine tempo swing, and the 55.7%/+2.3 IWD earns its early ALSA of 2.8. But it needs a Kithkin to behold — priority pick when the GW lane is open, otherwise a vanilla flash body.
Clachan Festival: The Kithkin build-around, but read the room — GW finished dead last because one removal spell stalls the go-wide plan. Three bodies for three plus a repeatable token engine is genuinely absurd IN Kithkin (56.5% WR, 78% play), but that number is conditioned on the deck; filler outside it.
Crib Swap: Flexible unconditional exile removal that hits any creature at instant speed — the giveback 1/1 changeling is a minor cost against a real threat. Flat ~50% GIH WR and -0.7 IWD understate it: this is your answer to bombs and lords, hold it rather than trade down. Solid removal, plays better than the number.
Curious Colossus: Premium bomb finisher — a 7/7 that also neuters your opponent's best creature into a vanilla 1/1 on entry. The 66.1% drawn WR (well above its opening-hand number) marks it as the late-game haymaker it is: a body plus removal in the format's grindy midrange. Take highly.
Eirdu, Carrier of Dawn: Bomb — first-pickable in any white deck. A 5-mana 5/5 flying lifelink is already premium, and giving your creature spells convoke plus a two-sided transform engine pushes 61% GIH / +9.6 IWD with an 88% play rate. Take it and build around it.
Encumbered Reejerey: Premium two-drop and near-universal include (85% play, 56.4% GIH, +1.7 IWD off an ALSA of 3.6). The -1/-1 counters shed as it taps, so it grows into a 5/4 while doubling as free blight removal. Slam it in Merfolk or any white deck.
Evershrike's Gift: Filler evasion aura — +1/+0 and flying for one mana with graveyard recursion if you're blighting. 53.2% GIH and negative IWD say it's not moving the needle; the recur clause only matters in a dedicated BW/RW blight shell. Marginal aggro-only playable, not a priority.
Flock Impostor: Excellent common-slot glue. Flash-flying changeling that bounces your own ETB creature (or saves one from removal) at instant speed, and it satisfies every typal payoff. 55% GIH and 83% play rate mark it as a flexible, always-maindeckable tempo piece.
Gallant Fowlknight: Playable combat trick on a body, best in aggressive Kithkin (GW). The team pump plus first strike can blow out a block or push lethal, but the -0.6 IWD and 49% play rate say it's a filler build-around that rewards a wide board — a fine last playable, not a pick you reach for.
Goldmeadow Nomad: Trap. The poster child for exciting-looking commons that don't play Magic — a 1/2 for W whose graveyard token payoff is far too slow to matter. Negative IWD (-1.7) and LoL's flat "don't draft" confirm it. Leave it in the pack even in Kithkin.
Keep Out: Conditional removal — only kills tapped creatures, so it's an ambush/attack-punisher, not proactive removal, plus enchantment destruction mode. The 52.6% WR and slightly negative IWD reflect the tapped restriction; fine playable in flash/tempo decks that force attacks, mediocre elsewhere. Solid role-player, not premium.
Kinbinding: Rare bomb engine for go-wide/Kithkin decks. It manufactures a token every combat and pumps your whole team by how many creatures entered that turn, snowballing fast — the 64.3% GIH and +12.2 IWD are elite. Best in GW/Wx tokens but wins on its own.
Kinsbaile Aspirant: One-drop lord-lite for GW Kithkin, mediocre elsewhere. LoL notes it's cheap-but-rarely-played and terrifying only when it curves out; the 58% GIH is inflated by the built-around Kithkin deck. Its 62% OH / 55% GD split confirms it wants to come down turn one and snowball, not be drawn late.
Kinscaer Sentry: Bomb-tier white two-drop: first strike lifelink for two is already fine, and the attack trigger cheats fatties into play tapped-and-attacking for free tempo. The +5.6 IWD and 59% GIH are elite for a rare that snowballs any go-wide board. First-pick it.
Kithkeeper: Seven-mana Vivid payoff that flops a 3/3 plus a token per color you control, with a tap-three pump. The +3.7 IWD comes from Vivid/multicolor decks stacking colors; in a two-color deck it's a mediocre topend. Role-player when your colors are wide, cuttable otherwise.
Liminal Hold: Premium removal and the best white common. Four-mana exile of any nonland permanent with 2 life attached, no real drawback — LoL's confirmed top white common. The 55.8% WR undersells it since removal doesn't win by being drawn; prioritize highly.
Meanders Guide: Low-priority Merfolk (UW) reanimator. Needs another untapped Merfolk to attack AND a MV-3-or-less target in the yard — too much setup, and both experts cooled on it after early access ("wasn't very impressed"). The 54% WR is the built-around Merfolk deck's number; take it late as a synergy piece.
Moonlit Lamenter: Premier white blight payoff and a legitimate early pick. Effectively a three-mana 1/4 that cantrips on arrival, then keeps drawing as you feed it counters — the 2/5 base dodges most removal. LoL's "this card is broken" plus +2.9 IWD and 71% play back the best white non-rare blight card.
Morningtide's Light: A tempo blowout / pseudo-Fog: exile a swarm of attackers or blockers, prevent all damage to you until your next turn, and they come back tapped for your alpha strike. The 8-point OH/GD split (49% opening, 57% drawn) shows it's a reactive answer you want to draw into, not keep. Strong at parrying aggro and closing — a real mythic.
Personify: Solid role-player, not a slam. Reuse an ETB (blink your Shinestriker/Deceit) and net a changeling body that feeds every typal payoff, at instant speed to dodge removal — but the flat +0.9 IWD and 5.0 ALSA say it's a build-around glue card, best where you have real ETBs to loop.
Protective Response: Premium removal — near-unconditional destroy at instant speed, and convoke plus the attacking/blocking clause make it cheap in creature decks. 57% GIH and a huge 89% play rate; LoL calls it clean interaction that also triggers Merfolk tap payoffs. High pick in any white deck.
Pyrrhic Strike: Flexible premium removal — a near-auto-include at 88.6% play, 58.3% GIH, +4.1 IWD. Blight 2 to hit both a creature (MV 3+) and an artifact/enchantment, or split it. Answers most real threats and the format's aura-removal. High pick.
Reluctant Dounguard: A 4/4 for three that arrives as a 2/2 and only grows if you keep flooding creatures onto the board. Negative IWD (-1.5) and 40% play flag it as a trap outside a fast go-wide GW/Kithkin deck — the counters rarely clear fast enough. Low-end filler.
Rhys, the Evermore: A support rare, not a bomb. Flash persist protects a creature through combat or removal and the counter-removal ability plays into blight, but a 2/2 for two with no immediate board impact posts a soft 52.7% — solid value glue in counters/blight, not a first-pick beating.
Riverguard's Reflexes: Filler combat trick. +2/+2, first strike, and untap can ambush an attacker or push damage, but at -1.0 IWD and a 23.9% play rate it's the definition of a trick that doesn't make most decks. Sideboard/last-slot; only in a dedicated tempo build.
Shore Lurker: Fine filler flyer for UW tempo — a 3/3 evasive body with a throwaway surveil that curves and chips in. GIH 53.7% with a flat IWD says it's a body you're happy to play but never excited to draft; take real cards over it.
Slumbering Walker: Excellent white rare: a 4/7 for five that dodges every removal benchmark and grinds by reanimating a small creature each turn as counters come off. 59.4% GIH WR, +5.9 IWD, 84% play — the toughness-7 body plus recursion engine wins attrition wars. Early pick in any white deck, backbreaking in grindy BW/BG.
Spiral into Solitude: Hard split card. As LoL frames it, if blight-1 is genuine upside for you (BW/RB), 'pay 2W to exile a creature and blight one' is insane premium removal; if it isn't, this is near-unplayable pacifism. The flat 0.0 IWD is the average of those two camps — draft it only when your deck wants counters.
Sun-Dappled Celebrant: Solid role-player top-end. A 5/6 vigilance for six that convoke discounts hard is a real body that blocks flyers and holds the ground in this high-toughness format; five toughness dodges Cinder Strike math. Middling 53% GIH reflects it being a curve-filler, not a bomb — fine playable, not a priority.
Thoughtweft Imbuer: The 0/5 body is the real payoff here, not the Kithkin pump — it walls the format's aggressive starts (dodges most combat) and overperformed as top uncommon. 58.3% GIH and +4.2 IWD even though the attack-alone clause rarely goes off. Strong defensive pickup in GW or any white deck.
Timid Shieldbearer: Solid aggressive two-drop: a 2/2 that turns your late-game excess mana into an anthem, giving Kithkin/weenie decks reach. 55.1% GIH at 70% play is a real workhorse for W beatdown; the pump is expensive but keeps it relevant in stalls. Fine early pick for aggro.
Tributary Vaulter: UW merfolk role-player. The 1/3 flyer is a fine blocker, but the tap-trigger pump only matters in a dedicated merfolk tempo shell — hence the 6.3 ALSA and 59% play rate. Good 55% GIH is conditioned on the built-around deck; a marginal filler elsewhere.
Wanderbrine Preacher: The premier Merfolk (UW) two-drop, but a trap outside the tribe. It leaks life every time tap synergies fire, which is great in the convoke/tap deck — 56.2% OH WR reflects the built-around body. In a slow or non-Merfolk deck it's a 2/2 that does nothing; prioritize only when UW is your lane.
Wanderbrine Trapper: Sleeper premium for UW merfolk/tap decks — one white for a repeatable tapper that clears blockers or locks down a threat every turn. The tap-another cost fits a wide board, and the numbers are loud: 59.5% GIH, +4.2 IWD, 84% play. Prioritize it in UW.
Winnowing: Not a sweeper — LoL flags it hard. It leaves each player one creature of a chosen type plus everything sharing that type, so tribal boards and changelings blank it completely. The 8-point OH/GD split (48%/56%) says it whiffs when you're behind and shines as a one-sided pseudo-wrath only when you're wide against a narrow board. Situational, know what it does.
Aquitect's Defenses: Combat trick / protection filler. Flash hexproof plus +1/+2 blanks a removal spell or wins a fight, but two-for-one risk and the tiny 21% play rate mark it as a sideboard-y trick, not a maindeck staple. Fine in tempo UW when you're the beatdown.
Blossombind: Serviceable UW/Vivid tempo removal. LoL's "best Claustrophobia ever" got walked back — first copy is C+, extras rot, it leaves the body on board (bad for Vivid) and blight decks untap around it. 55% GIH is real but soft; take one as pseudo-removal, don't stack them.
Champions of the Shoal: Merfolk bomb — the numbers are outstanding (62.4% GIH, +9.9 IWD, ALSA 2.6). Repeatable tap-and-stun on every ETB and tap locks down a blocker or attacker each turn, and the behold cost even recurs your exiled Merfolk. First-pick in UW; needs Merfolk fodder to cast.
Disruptor of Currents: Premium UW tempo — flash convoke a 3/3 for as little as blue mana while bouncing any nonland permanent, effectively a two-for-one at instant speed. 61.2% GIH, +8.4 IWD, 88% play: it's the merfolk deck's engine. Slam it in blue tempo.
Flitterwing Nuisance: Strong early pickup, borderline bomb in tempo/fairies. A one-mana flyer that turns your whole board into a card-draw engine — 60% GIH, +8 IWD, and a 2.4 ALSA all confirm it overperforms. Snap it up in UB/UW aggressive builds.
Glamer Gifter: Excellent uncommon and a UB Fairies staple. Flash flyer that turns a creature into a 4/4 blocks-everything changeling ambushes combat, flips a race, and even satisfies typal counts — the +3.2 IWD and 82.5% play rate confirm the read. High pick in any blue deck; premium in Fairies.
Glamermite: Serviceable flash flyer that plays best as a Fairies/flash role-player — a 2/2 you deploy on the opponent's turn to steal a combat or unlock an attacker. Mediocre 33.9% play and modest WR mark it as a synergy piece, not a maindeck lock outside UB/UW.
Glen Elendra Guardian: Strong UB/Fairies rare: a flash-flying 3/3 (enters 2/3) that ambushes and later counters a noncreature spell while replacing itself. 56.6% GIH WR, 86% play — the flash body alone is playable and the counter is a free tempo swing. Premium in flash decks, good creature anywhere blue.
Glen Elendra's Answer: Powerful but conditional blowout — an uncounterable Overload counter that sweeps a whole turn's worth of spells/abilities and rebuilds your board with Faerie flyers. The 59.3% GIH is dragged down by dead early draws (65% play rate, sits until you have targets); a devastating top-end in UB Fairies/flash.
Gravelgill Scoundrel: Sneaky-good UW Merfolk common — Ben whiffed it at zero, retro flipped it to "one of the most important Merfolk commons." The tap-to-be-unblockable clause turns it into repeatable evasive damage and triggers tap payoffs; with Bark of Doran it's a 4/4 unblockable. High pick in the Merfolk lane.
Harmonized Crescendo: Convoke draw payoff that's a wheel-able role-player, not a bomb: 53.2% GIH and a flat +0.1 IWD say it whiffs without a wide tribal board. In a committed Merfolk/Kithkin go-wide deck it refuels for cheap; elsewhere it's a clunky six-mana do-nothing.
Illusion Spinners: Evasive but overpriced: a 4/3 flyer with untapped-hexproof, flashable only if you already have a Faerie. 51.2% GIH and 30% play mark it as a Fairies-only role-player — the hexproof protects it but five mana for a 4/3 is below curve. Playable filler in UB/UR faeries.
Kulrath Mystic: "Looks bad, plays great" — LoL's Sahaguin comp. The 2/4 blanks two-drops and the threat-of-activation makes it unblockable and a fine defender in Elementals or Vivid. Low 34% play rate drags perception, but the 53.9% GIH earns a maindeck slot in the right deck.
Loch Mare: Bomb. A {1}{U} 4/5 that's a repeatable card-draw and tap-down engine once the -1/-1 counters come off — 62.1% GIH, +9.3 IWD, first-pick ALSA of 1.7. Flexible, self-sufficient, wins grindy games on its own. Slam it P1P1.
Lofty Dreams: Better than most auras because it cantrips and convokes — draw a card, then +2/+2 and flying on a body, castable cheaply off a wide board. Two-for-one insurance against the aura blowout makes it a fine UW/convoke playable at 55% GIH; still a role-player, not a bomb.
Mirrorform: A mythic dream that mostly reads as a splashy 6-mana build-around: turn your whole board into copies of your best creature (or an opponent's). 55.5% GIH WR with a 50%/59% OH/GD split — dead in your opener, a blowout when you've built the board. Fun ceiling, but a real playable, not a bomb; you need bodies down first.
Noggle the Mind: Efficient pseudo-removal at flash speed — shrink their bomb to a 1/1 vanilla, neutralizing lords, evasion, and abilities for two mana. The 55.2% GIH and 76% play rate confirm it's a reliable answer, though it leaves a body on board so hold it for their best threat rather than trading down.
Oko, Lorwyn Liege: Bomb planeswalker — cheap at three mana, protects itself with -2/-0, and the transformed side mills for value and makes two 3/3 Elks. 56% GIH understates it because the number spans off-color decks; the 1.8 ALSA and 81% play rate show drafters correctly grab it early. First-pick.
Omni-Changeling: Flexible blue uncommon that copies your best creature and stays a changeling for every typal payoff, plus convoke to deploy it early. Ben's top blue uncommon, though 17Lands (56% GIH, +2.5 IWD) puts it below the hype — solid but not a slam. Best in Merfolk/Elementals.
Pestered Wellguard: Strong UW tempo three-drop that spits out a flying Faerie every time it taps — great with convoke, tapping payoffs, and attacks. 54.5% GIH and 78% play at a 4.1 ALSA make it a reliable merfolk/faerie glue card. Prioritize in tap-synergy blue.
Rime Chill: Vivid-only tempo. At full six-plus mana it's a double-tap-plus-stun-plus-cantrip, but you need a wide color spread to make it playable — the 47.8% OH vs 55% GD split shows it's dead early and fine late. Playable role-player in 2c Vivid, unremarkable elsewhere.
Rimefire Torque: Trap / near-unplayable. Needs a heavy typal board to charge, then only copies your next instant/sorcery — three counters for one copy is far too slow. The 40.1% WR and 4.3% play rate are damning; leave it in the box.
Rimekin Recluse: Best blue uncommon and a slam — a 3/2 for three that bounces any creature is pure tempo, resetting an ETB or undoing a blocker. LoL: "bonkers as advertised." The stats scream it (60.2% GIH, +6.6 IWD, 90% play); great in both Merfolk and Elementals.
Run Away Together: Weak double-bounce — it forces you to bounce one of your own creatures alongside theirs, a symmetric tempo wash. Lowest play rate here (22.5%), 7.2 ALSA and negative IWD confirm it's near-unplayable maindeck. Sideboard/filler tempo card at best; leave it in the pack.
Shinestriker: Premium blue card — LoL ranks it the #1 Vivid payoff and says it belongs in every blue deck regardless of Vivid count: 'Mulldrifter is still good in 2026.' A 3/3 flyer that refills your hand; take it high anywhere blue, and it only gets better with more colors.
Silvergill Mentor: Premium UW Merfolk two-drop — a 2/1 that makes a 1/1 Merfolk token is two bodies plus a lord-count for two mana, and behold is trivial in the tribe. 60% GIH / +5.2 IWD / 62% OH mark it as a proactive, always-good early play. High pick when you're in Merfolk.
Silvergill Peddler: Marginal filler at 52.5% play and a flat +0.0 IWD — the tap-loot needs to trigger repeatedly to matter, and a 2/3 that doesn't attack profitably rarely gets there. A reasonable Merfolk body with light card-selection upside, but replaceable.
Spell Snare: Narrow counter — only hits mana-value-2 spells, so it whiffs whole turns. Sub-50% GIH and 13.5% play confirm it's a sideboard/metagame card in this grindy format where you can't leave blue up on a hunch. Leave it in the pool most drafts.
Stratosoarer: Reliable Elementals common. Five toughness dodges the format's removal, it grants evasion on ETB, and basic landcycling means it's never a dead card. 54.7% GIH with a healthy +2.9 IWD — a flexible curve-filler and fixing smoother for UR.
Summit Sentinel: Excellent Vivid glue and a fine blocker anywhere. A {1}{U} 1/3 that cantrips on death is a perfect board-staller — high toughness holds the ground, and neither player wants to trade with it. LoL's "perfect vivid piece" read matches the 53.7% WR; a happy early-to-mid pick in UR/Vivid.
Sunderflock: Format-warping finisher that fell just short of "I win" — cost-reduced by your biggest Elemental, it Evacuations all non-Elementals while your board (and changelings) stay. LoL calls it A-minus not A because changelings dodge the bounce, but 64% GIH and +13 IWD make it a first-pick bomb in UR.
Swat Away: LoL calls it a strong Elementals counter/removal — costs {2} less when you're being attacked, so it's often a 2-mana Remand-plus that also answers creatures by tucking them. 54.7% WR, 67% play; the discount rewards being the defender, which fits UR midrange. Solid flexible answer, better than its color's usual counters.
Sygg, Wanderwine Wisdom: Rare bomb in UW Merfolk. An unblockable 2/2 that turns any creature into a repeatable card-draw or protection engine each turn via the flip — 60.6% GIH, +8.8 IWD, and it curves out turn two. First-pickable and a signpost into the A-tier merfolk lane.
Tanufel Rimespeaker: Secret-gold-card of the format — a 2/4 that cantrips off every 4+ MV spell you cast. LoL's retro flips Ethan's D to "goes in any deck, not just elementals": the toughness blocks well and the card advantage snowballs in a grindy format. Strong uncommon, higher than it looks.
Temporal Cleansing: Strong tempo removal that convokes toward zero: tuck-second-from-top blanks the target for a turn while you're ahead. 56.1% GIH but the +1.4 IWD and 53% OH WR flag it's better the more aggressive you are — it buys time, not permanent answers. High pick in UW tempo, softer in grindy decks.
Thirst for Identity: Instant-speed card advantage: draw three, keep all if you pitch a creature, otherwise net one. 53.2% GIH is fine but unspectacular — in a creature-heavy ECL deck it's usually a clean +1 with selection. Solid blue role-player, not a high pick.
Unexpected Assistance: Top blue common. Convoke turns Draw-three-discard-one into a potentially free refuel that's backbreaking in the convoke/tempo UW shell. Confirmed premium by LoL; the 55.8% GIH understates a card-advantage engine you should draft highly.
Unwelcome Sprite: Strong UB Fairies/Flash payoff. A 2/1 flyer that surveils 2 every time you act on the opponent's turn rewards exactly the flash-dense deck you want to be — +2.8 IWD, 74% play rate. Evasive clock plus card selection; high pick when flash is your plan, a fine flyer otherwise.
Wanderwine Distracter: Cut it. A 4/3 whose -3/-0 only triggers when it taps means you're attacking into blockers to shrink one, and it does nothing defensively. Sub-51% GIH, negative IWD, and 19.7% play confirm it's near-unplayable even in Merfolk.
Wanderwine Farewell: Convoke-fueled multi-bounce that pays off Merfolk with 1/1 tokens per permanent returned — a tempo swing that rebuilds your board. 56.8% GIH WR, 67% play; convoke makes the seven-mana cost far cheaper in a wide UW deck. Good in Merfolk, a fine tempo card elsewhere blue, but wants the tribe to hit ceiling.
Wild Unraveling: Niche counterspell. UU Cancel that can cost blight-2 instead of a mana, giving Merfolk/UW a rare way to interact with Vivid decks' key payoffs, per LoL — but the 25% play rate and 7.2 ALSA mark it as a maindeck-optional interaction piece, not a staple. Board it in against bombs.
Auntie's Sentence: Solid flexible RB/black removal — the -2/-2 mode kills most early creatures while the discard mode strips a threat, so it's never dead. LoL notes it beats other split cards because the back half is removal, not a vanilla body; overperformed on camera. Good playable, prioritize the removal use.
Barbed Bloodletter: Fringe combat trick disguised as equipment — flash it in, grant wither, and blow out a block or snipe a small creature via -1/-1 counters. But 18.4% play and ALSA 7.4 say it's a late-table filler; the +1/+2 buff rarely justifies the card. Sideboard/situational.
Bile-Vial Boggart: Sticky one-drop Goblin that trades up and leaves a -1/-1 counter behind — Ethan's pet common. The 51.9% GIH undersells it in RB goblins, where the type and the death-trigger removal feed the grindy blight-drain plan. Good early-curve piece in the archetype.
Bitterbloom Bearer: Bomb. A two-mana flash-flyer that builds a flying army every upkeep for a trivial life cost — 57.9% GIH, +6.6 IWD, and a 1.9 ALSA that screams first-pick. Inevitability in UB fairies and a fine standalone flyer anywhere. Take it.
Blight Rot: Good removal but heavily contested and diminishing. Four -1/-1 counters kills most things and enables blight synergies, yet five-toughness bodies shrug it off and it leaves fodder for Vivid — Ethan's "C+ then C-" nails it. First copy is a solid pick at 55.4%; don't stack them.
Blighted Blackthorn: Legitimate late-pick value in blight decks — a 3/7 wall that dodges everything at five toughness and can draw cards by blighting onto a spent two-drop. LoL flags it as a big riser: "the wheel is alive with pick 10." Never a high pick, but a fine BW/RB grinder.
Bloodline Bidding: Convoke mass-reanimation build-around — return every creature of one type from your graveyard, backbreaking in Elves/tribal after a stall. 58.6% GIH WR and +4.8 IWD, but that number is conditioned on the deck that fills the yard and floods bodies; convoke plus a full graveyard makes the {6}{B}{B} realistic. Top-end payoff for BG/RB grind, mediocre in a deck that can't feed it.
Boggart Mischief: Strong RB Goblins engine. Blight-1 to make two Goblin tokens, then every Goblin death drains a life and gains you one — exactly the grindy blight-drain plan the guild wants. The 57% GIH is the built-around number; excellent in RB, unplayable outside it.
Boggart Prankster: Filler RB Goblin. A 1/3 that only pumps attacking Goblins is a build-around anthem-lite with no floor outside the tribe; 52% GIH and a sub-45% play rate flag it as a marginal aggro piece. Playable only in dedicated Goblins, and even there it's near the bottom.
Bogslither's Embrace: Format-defining black common: one-mana exile-any-creature when blight is upside (it usually is in BW/RB). "Absurd" per LoL, and 88% play with +2.9 IWD backs it despite GIH underrating removal. Premium — take it near the top.
Champion of the Weird: RB goblins bomb — LoL calls it "broken in half." The behold cost is trivial in the tribe, and a 5/5 with a repeatable target-opponent-blights-2 plague effect is inevitability. 59.5% GIH and +8.8 IWD from the built-around deck. Take it and commit to Goblins.
Creakwood Safewright: "Tarmogoyf for two" in elves. Enters as a 2/2 but climbs to 3/3+ the same end step once an elf hits your yard, and BG fills graveyards fast. 57.2% GIH and 83% play rate confirm the ceiling — a premium BG two-drop, merely a body in non-elf decks.
Darkness Descends: Niche board wipe, mostly sideboard. Two -1/-1 counters to each creature is symmetric and only 4 mana of value if you're ahead on go-wide or high-toughness bodies — 49.1% WR and 16.7% play rate show it rarely makes the cut. Playable in a dedicated blight/token shell, filler elsewhere.
Dawnhand Dissident: Elite BG rare and an early pick — one black for a repeatable surveil/graveyard-hate engine that recurs your best exiled creatures by paying counters. It's slow to snowball but the ceiling is inevitability; 58.9% GIH, +6.2 IWD, 86% play confirm it's a build-around that just wins grindy games.
Dawnhand Eulogist: LoL's "banger for the elf deck" — a 3/3 menace that mills three and drains 2 whenever an Elf's in the yard (nearly always in BG). 57.9% GIH WR; the drain plus evasion make it a real threat that also fuels Unbury/recursion. Strong common in Elves, playable filler elsewhere black — the number rises in-tribe.
Dose of Dawnglow: Overcosted reanimation, a trap outside dedicated builds. Five mana to return a creature is slow, and the blight-2 rider only triggers off your turn — the negative -0.7 IWD and 51% GIH say it underdelivers. Only run it if you have expensive bodies worth cheating back and blight synergy.
Dream Seizer: Streaky UB Fairies flyer — a 3/2 evasive body that can blight one of your own to strip the opponent's hand. LoL loved it in early access but the retro "wish it had a home" tag and a soft 51% GIH / 27% play rate show it's inconsistent; the sub-49% OH means it wants a longer game. Fine role-player, not a staple.
Gloom Ripper: Elf bomb, full stop — 66.2% GIH and +13.0 IWD are among the set's best. The double-Elf pump/shrink two-for-ones in combat and can outright kill a blocker while your 4/4 crashes in. First-pick in BG Elves; even a modest Elf count makes it swing games.
Gnarlbark Elm: The set's biggest fall from grace — reads as a blight payoff but plays as a glacially slow 3/2 (two -1/-1 counters) that takes an eternity to fire its -2/-2. The 54% GIH flatters it; Ethan wouldn't play it in most decks. Trap unless deep BW blight.
Graveshifter: Great flexible uncommon. Changeling that Raise Deads your best creature on a 2/2 body — enables recursion loops, counts as every type, and slots into any grindy deck. 87% play rate and Ethan's second-favorite black uncommon; a high-floor value card.
Grub, Storied Matriarch: Strong RB Goblins rare. A 2/1 menace that rebuys a Goblin on ETB, then flips to churn out attacking copies via blight — grindy card advantage exactly where Goblins wants it. 57.8% GIH, +6.9 IWD; a build-around engine that's an easy early pick in the RB lane.
Gutsplitter Gang: A serviceable beater that wants a blight home — a 6/6 for four is huge, but the upkeep tax means without counters to distribute you're bleeding 3 a turn. Merely average (51.9% GIH, +0.6 IWD) says it's a body, not a payoff; fine in RB/BW where the drawback is upside.
Heirloom Auntie: Trap two-drop: enters as a 2/2 (two -1/-1 counters) and only grows as your other creatures die, so it's a slow sacrifice-payoff that's dead without a steady death engine. 48.5% GIH WR, -2.4 IWD, 34% play — the numbers confirm it underperforms in most goblin builds. Sideboard/filler unless you're deep in a sacrifice shell.
Iron-Shield Elf: Filler two-drop, cut when you can. Both LoL analysts agree it's 'not that good even in Elves' — the 1 toughness dies to the format's ubiquitous 1/1 tokens and a Blight Rot/Cinder Strike, and discard-to-indestructible doesn't fix that. Numot calls it early filler; the green 3/1 surveiller is better.
Moonglove Extractor: Underrated BG Elf card-advantage engine — a 2/1 Scroll Thief that draws just by attacking, no connection needed. LoL's "how did I not love this" and the retro "can't sit with us" award both signal it plays better than the 52% GIH suggests; the negative IWD reflects the fragile 2/1 body. Decent grindy playable.
Moonshadow: One-mana 7/7 menace that unlocks by dumping cards to your graveyard — a mythic that rewards mill/sacrifice shells (Elves, Blight). Numbers are good-not-broken (57% GIH, +5.0 IWD) because it can sit inert as a small body if you can't feed the graveyard. High pick where you can flip it fast.
Mornsong Aria: Symmetric build-around enchantment that shuts off draws and lifegain while everyone tutors and bleeds — no Limited home. Null WR off 2.8% play says virtually nobody ran it and it didn't win. Sideboard/cube curio, unplayable in a normal ECL deck.
Mudbutton Cursetosser: Retro's biggest riser. A one-mana 2/1 (with a goblin) that trades then removes a small creature on death — aggressive tempo plus built-in removal that snowballs in RB goblins. 60.5% OH and +4.9 IWD; grab it, and pay the {2} tax freely when needed.
Nameless Inversion: Premium removal — best black uncommon. {1}{B} instant +3/-3 kills nearly anything, strips changeling types off a payoff, and doubles as a combat "lava spike" or an elf in your graveyard for BG. The GIH WR (56.4%) understates it since efficient removal doesn't win by being drawn. Take it very high.
Nightmare Sower: A niche Fairies/flash reward — 2/3 flying lifelink is a decent blocker, and the repeatable -1/-1 on your opponent's-turn spells accrues real value in a dedicated UB shell. Outside it the trigger rarely fires (40.8% play, 51.3% GIH); role-player that needs the flash density.
Perfect Intimidation: Worst card here — a clunky {3}{B} sorcery whose modes (opponent exiles two from hand, or strip counters off a creature) are both niche and low-impact for the cost. 47.4% GIH WR and a 10.5% play rate say drafters correctly cut it. Sideboard-only against specific counter/blight matchups.
Requiting Hex: Efficient but capped removal. One mana to kill anything MV 2-or-less, with optional blight-1 for 2 life — great early tempo against two-drops, but it whiffs on the high-toughness midrange bodies that define ECL. The middling 52.7% GIH reflects that ceiling; a fine playable, not premium.
Retched Wretch: Solid RB/blight two-drop — a 4/2 for three that recurs itself once if it dies with a -1/-1 counter, folding neatly into the blight-sacrifice game. 53% GIH and 56% play rate mark it a reliable aggressive body with built-in resilience. Good role-player, better in decks putting counters on it.
Scarblade Scout: Solid aggressive Elf common: 2/2 lifelink for two that mills two to feed the BG graveyard-as-resource plan. 57.4% GIH and 78% play make it a fine early body that supports Gloom Ripper and Midnight Tilling. Good role-player in Elves.
Scarblade's Malice: One-mana deathtouch + lifelink trick that also nets a 2/2 Elf if the creature dies — flexible combat and a removal enabler on any blocker. 54.1% GIH is respectable; the Elf token ties it to BG. Solid playable trick, best where you want the body.
Shimmercreep: Vivid drain payoff. Menace 3/5 is already a fine body, and in a wide color spread the ETB swings four-plus life. The 50% OH vs 57% GD split marks it as a build-around reward — strong in 2c Vivid/Blight, a vanilla beater in strict two-color.
Taster of Wares: Excellent Goblins (RB) rare — disruption plus card advantage. Even with one Goblin it strips their best card, and it can steal a spell to cast off any color. 60.6% GIH, +8.9 IWD, ALSA 2.8. Scales with your board and rarely dead; a top-tier pick in the Goblin lane.
Twilight Diviner: Strong BG rare engine — surveil 2 on entry fuels the graveyard, then it copies creatures you cast/return from the yard, snowballing every turn. It's a payoff that needs recursion to pop, but 56% GIH with 75% play shows it delivers in the Elf/graveyard deck; solid early pick in BG.
Unbury: Numot: "best card in its pack by a wide margin, not close" — flexible 2-mana recursion that buys back one creature or two sharing a type. 55.0% GIH WR, 81% play; card advantage stapled to tribal synergy, absurd in Elves and good in any creature-dense deck. High pick, take it over most commons.
Ashling, Rekindled: Rare bomb in UR Elementals. A 1/3 that loots on entry/flip and then flips into a ramp engine for your expensive spells — 60.5% GIH, +9.4 IWD, curves out turn two and enables the elemental top-end. Take it high; a season-long UR riser.
Boldwyr Aggressor: Narrow RW Giants payoff. A 2/5 double strike is a fine defensive body, but the anthem only matters with other Giants, and 26% play rate confirms that lane rarely materializes. GIH is inflated by the built-around games; a fringe uncommon outside dedicated Giants.
Boneclub Berserker: Goblin lord-lite that needs a full board to matter — a 2/4 for four that only threatens with two-plus other Goblins. 50.5% GIH, negative IWD, and 27.8% play mark it as replaceable filler even in RB. Playable only in a deep Goblin count.
Boulder Dash: Premium red removal — two mana to split 2 and 1 damage, killing an X/2 and pinging another. Numot rates it splash-worthy and 55.4% GIH understates removal that doesn't win by being drawn. Prioritize the first one or two; three copies is too many.
Brambleback Brute: "Neighborhood bully." A 4/5 for three (enters 2/3) that pushes its own damage through — a genuine RW/RG midrange threat both experts loved. The 30% play rate and 7.0 ALSA reflect its aggressive-deck niche, but the 4/5 mode overperforms; a fine beater.
Burning Curiosity: Strong card advantage in Blight/midrange red — a potential draw-three at common. Blight 1 to exile three is real gas for grindy RB/RW, filling the card gap Goblins lacks. But -0.1 IWD and 30.9% play rate show it's build-around, not universal, with steep diminishing returns; first copy only.
Champion of the Path: A dangerous UR payoff but build-your-deck-around-it — the behold cost demands another Elemental, and the real damage comes from chaining ETB Elementals to burn face. A 7/3 that recurs on death is fragile; 54.4% GIH and +4 IWD say good-not-great, contingent on Elemental density.
Cinder Strike: The format's best common, full stop (LoL/Numot). One mana, deal 4 to a creature by blighting one of your own — near-universal removal that answers everything under five toughness. GIH WR (55.7%) structurally UNDERrates it since removal doesn't win by being in hand; the 87% play rate and format consensus are the real signal. First-pick-caliber red common, prioritize it.
Collective Inferno: Trap. A 5-mana convoke enchantment that only doubles damage from one creature type does nothing the turn it lands and asks for a wide tribal board you'd rather just attack with — the negative -1.9 IWD and 48.6% GIH confirm it underperforms. Leave it in the pool.
Elder Auntie: Filler RB Goblin — a 2/2 that makes a 1/1 Goblin is two bodies for three mana, fine as go-wide fodder but unexciting. 52% GIH and 45% play rate peg it as replaceable filler; it does its best work feeding Goblin/sacrifice triggers rather than attacking. Low-priority playable.
End-Blaze Epiphany: Premium scalable removal with card advantage stapled on: X damage kills nearly anything, and the dead creature's power fuels an impulse-draw. 60.2% GIH and +7.8 IWD confirm it overperforms even the raw removal read. First-pick-caliber in any red deck.
Enraged Flamecaster: UR spells role-player: a 3/2 reach body that drains 2 whenever you cast a four-plus-drop. 52.8% GIH and 42% play mean it's a fine filler in a spell-dense elementals deck and unplayable elsewhere — the reach at least blocks flyers. Middle-of-the-pack.
Explosive Prodigy: Premium Vivid removal on a body. In a two-plus color deck the ETB is Shock-or-better attached to a creature, scaling to a full board-wipe of a threat late. 58% GIH, +5.6 IWD, 85% play — a top-tier UR/Vivid pickup that removal WR still undersells.
Feed the Flames: Premium removal. 5 damage at instant speed that exiles is bread-and-butter interaction — kills all but the five-toughness club, dodges recursion, and answers bombs. The 54.4% GIH understates it per the format's removal caveat; the +2.4 IWD and 79.9% play rate are the truer signal. Take it high in any red deck.
Flame-Chain Mauler: Underrated aggressive two-drop that shines in a two-drop-scarce format. The pump-plus-menace threat-of-activation makes it effectively unblockable late, and it carries the Elemental type for UR. LoL flags it as wheeling despite being good; a fine early beater at 53% GIH.
Flamebraider: Kill-on-sight per LoL — a 2/2 that taps for two mana toward Elemental spells/abilities, ramping UR Elementals into absurd starts. 62.7% OH WR (best-in-class opening-hand number) shows how explosive it is when curved out early. Snap-pick in UR, and deny it to the Elemental drafter even if you're not playing it.
Flamekin Gildweaver: Solid midrange common. A 4/3 trample for four that leaves a Treasure — respectable body plus fixing/ramp toward your top-end or splash, and the 56.5% GIH backs a maindeck slot. Better in Vivid/Treasure (RG) decks that convert the Treasure into value; otherwise a fine curve-filler.
Giantfall: Solid red removal via fight-lite — your creature deals its power to theirs with no damage back to you, plus a relevant artifact-destroy mode. 64% play rate and +2 IWD show it's a real removal spell in creature decks, though it needs a body and whiffs if you're behind. Good playable, prioritize when your curve is beefy.
Goatnap: Trap/near-unplayable: 48.4% GIH, 43% OH WR, and 5.5% play. A one-turn Threaten with a Goat rider that rarely triggers — no sacrifice outlet means you just get a temporary attacker. Leave it in the sideboard barring a dedicated sac shell.
Goliath Daydreamer: UR spells engine on a 4/4 for four — every instant/sorcery you cast gets exiled and re-cast free when it attacks, snowballing fast. 55.2% GIH with a pick-3 ALSA; the ceiling is huge in a deck with cheap interaction. Strong build-around rare, take it in blue-red.
Gristle Glutton: "Broken in blight decks." A 1/3 that rummages while feeding -1/-1 counters onto your blight payoffs every turn — a free repeatable enabler. The 53.8% GIH is deceptively low because its value is engine-based; a high pick in RB/BW blight, filler outside it.
Hexing Squelcher: Mediocre rare despite the play rate. A 2/2 for two that grants your team ward is anti-counter/anti-removal tech, but the ward tax is weak and the body dies to everything — 50.7% GIH, -0.6 IWD say the protection rarely pays off. A filler early drop, not a reason to be in red.
Impolite Entrance: Trap — a one-mana trample/haste cantrip that reads like a combat trick but does almost nothing to a board. 43.6% GIH, -4.5 IWD, and 9.8% play make it one of the worst cards you can register. Don't play it.
Kindle the Inner Flame: Elemental payoff — a temporary hasty copy of your best creature for burst/ETB value, with flashback that behold-fuels late. 55.3% GIH WR but only 40% play and a 6.3 ALSA: a build-around that wants a big ETB creature and an Elemental-dense deck. Good in UR Elementals, unexciting elsewhere.
Kulrath Zealot: Excellent Elementals top-end, LoL's 'clunky-overperformer' nominee — the key 5 toughness dodges Blight Rot/Seer/Cinder Strike, it draws a card on entry, and it landcycles when you're flooded or off-color. 56.7% GIH on a six-drop is strong; a high pick for UR and a fine curve-topper anywhere red.
Lasting Tarfire: Trap. A 2-mana enchantment that only pings for two if you put a counter on a creature that turn — narrow, do-nothing-to-the-board reach that the format punishes. The 47% GIH / -3.5 IWD / 44% OH are damning. Sideboard at best, even in blight/counters decks.
Lavaleaper: Trap rare — symmetric haste helps the opponent too, and the ramp clause is win-more. 48.6% GIH, negative IWD, and 11.2% play confirm the 4/4-for-four body doesn't earn its slot. Skip it unless you have a specific haste-alpha-strike combo.
Meek Attack: Build-around enchantment that blinks small creatures for a hasty attack then sacrifices them — no payoff density in ECL Limited. Null WR off under 1% play confirms it was never deck-worthy. Skip; pure Constructed/cube fodder.
Reckless Ransacking: Filler combat trick. +3/+2 plus a Treasure is card-neutral tempo, but the format punishes durdly tricks and the 50.1% GIH with a 10.7% play rate says most decks correctly cut it. Sideboard/last-slot material for aggressive Treasure builds only.
Scuzzback Scrounger: Good aggressive Goblin (RB) two-drop. A 3/2 for two that optionally ramps/fixes via Treasure while enabling blight is a clean curve-filler with upside. 55.1% GIH and a strong 57.2% OH WR mark it as an early-game body that plays well proactively; solid pick in the Goblin lane.
Sear: Premium removal and a top pick — two mana, instant, 4 damage kills nearly everything at ECL's toughness range including blight targets. Ben's #1 red uncommon; remember GIH underrates removal, so its 56.7% (90% play, 2.9 ALSA) undersells how high you should be taking it. Hold it for lords.
Sizzling Changeling: Solid Vivid/tribal glue: a 3/2 changeling that satisfies every typal payoff and counts red+colorless pips, and replaces itself on death with card advantage. LoL likes it as a base-red Vivid piece opponents don't want to kill. 54.1% WR, 83% play — a reliable body that keeps you open across archetypes.
Soul Immolation: Bomb sweeper-plus-reach for blight decks. Blight X to deal X to each opponent AND all their creatures — a one-sided board wipe that also closes the game, scaling off your highest toughness. Elite 63.2% GIH / +11.9 IWD; best in BW/RB where you have big-toughness bodies to fuel it, but format-warping when it fires.
Soulbright Seeker: Marginal UR Elemental one-drop. A 2/1 for R with a trample-granting mana sink is fine early aggression, and behold is easy in Elementals, but the ability rarely swings games; 55% GIH is decent for a one-drop. Playable role-player in the Elemental lane, low pick elsewhere.
Sourbread Auntie: Excellent RB Goblin uncommon: three bodies for four mana when blight is upside, and even at face it's a 4/3 plus two 1/1 Goblins. "Nuts" per LoL; 55.3% GIH understates it because the go-wide value shines in a built Goblin deck. High pick in RB.
Spinerock Tyrant: Top-tier bomb — a 6/6 flying wither Dragon that copies your single-target spells (removal, tricks) with wither attached. 61.8% GIH, +11.5 IWD, pick-2 ALSA: it ends games on its own and doubles your interaction. First-pick, splash if you must.
Squawkroaster: Vivid finisher. Double strike on a */4 means it hits like a truck in a wide deck (4 colors = 8 damage) but is a limp 1/4 in two colors — the 50.2% OH vs 53% GD gap confirms it's a payoff, not a slam. Playable ceiling in 2c Vivid, cuttable elsewhere.
Sting-Slinger: Marginal Goblins payoff. A 3/3 that pings both opponents by consuming your own board is slow and mana-hungry — the -0.3 IWD and 56% play rate say the reach rarely justifies the activation. Playable in a go-wide blight/goblin deck as a finisher engine; filler otherwise.
Tweeze: Below-the-bar burn that the experts sour on — three mana for 3 to any target with a loot rider is clunky and off-curve for Elementals (not MV 4). Ben and Ethan agree it's not worth it. 54.6% GIH is inflated by being removal-ish; a mediocre filler removal spell, playable but low.
Warren Torchmaster: LoL calls it "a house" for blight decks — a 2/2 that offers a FREE blight-1 each combat (granting haste), fueling Cinder Strike, blight payoffs, and counter-removal shenanigans every turn. But note the split: 51.1% GIH WR and negative IWD show it's mediocre OUTSIDE a built blight shell. Take highly in RB/RW blight, cut it if you're not counter-synergy.
Assert Perfection: The most contested green common — Ethan calls it the best, Ben says it's way worse than Cinder Strike or Luminal Hold, and the retro dubbed it the 'skill-issue' card that punishes you but rarely wins games. A conditional fight/removal needing a creature and good board state; the 57.9% GIH says it's a real playable, but hold it and don't over-value it.
Aurora Awakener: Bomb finisher for Vivid — a 7/7 trample that cascades multiple permanents onto the battlefield off your color count, an ETB that wins the game on the spot. 60% GIH, +10.5 IWD, 1.7 ALSA and 91% play rate; the huge IWD confirms it swings games hard. First-pick in any multicolor deck.
Bloom Tender: Vivid mana mythic that fixes and ramps hard in multicolor/Vivid shells — its ceiling is three-plus mana of any color on turn three. Modest 54.3% GIH and +3.4 IWD because it's a fragile 1/1 that invites removal, but the ceiling is bomb-level in a greedy deck. Early pick if you're going Vivid.
Blossoming Defense: Ben's #1 green uncommon — one mana for +2/+2 and hexproof, the premier way to protect engines and win combat in a format that punishes losing your key piece. 55.6% GIH undersells a trick every green deck wants. High pick, especially with a bomb to shield.
Bristlebane Battler: Strong rare, effectively a bomb in creature decks. A trample-ward 6/6 for two that shrinks its counters as you deploy bodies — often a 4/4+ within a turn or two. 63.6% OH, +6.3 IWD, 2.0 ALSA; play any creature-dense deck and it's a snap first pick.
Bristlebane Outrider: Five-toughness hero. A 3/5 that dodges Blight Rot, Cinder Strike, and the Seer while pressuring as an evasive 5/5 with any second creature — LoL's "great body" is dead on. 56.1% GIH; a reliable, removal-resistant midrange body that overperforms in BG/token shells. Strong pick.
Celestial Reunion: A flexible tutor whose ceiling is a free creature onto the battlefield when you pay the behold cost and hit your type — great in a focused tribal deck, mediocre as a fetch-to-hand elsewhere. The near-flat +0.7 IWD and 48.8% play show it's often just an expensive Diabolic Tutor; deck-dependent.
Champions of the Perfect: Bomb-tier Elf rare — a 6/6 for four that draws a card off every creature spell you cast, with the behold-an-Elf cost returning to hand when it dies. Best numbers in the chunk: 61.0% GIH WR, +8.3 IWD, 2.0 ALSA, 85% play. Runaway card advantage on a huge body; first-pick in BG Elves, splashable anywhere.
Chomping Changeling: Below-replacement even as a changeling. A 1/2 for three whose destroy-artifact/enchantment ETB is often a dead mode, and the negative -3.3 IWD and sub-50% GIH confirm it drags. The typal upside doesn't save a bad body; play it only if you're desperate for changeling count.
Crossroads Watcher: Strong green common — a 3/3 trample that pumps whenever another creature enters creates real threat-of-activation blocking math. LoL calls it a functional reprint of a Foundations top common and "a huge problem you have to block." Good in GW/Kithkin and any go-wide green deck; reliable playable.
Dawn's Light Archer: Serviceable flash body — a 4/2 reach for three that ambushes attackers or trades up at instant speed. Flat performance (54.8% GIH, -0.6 IWD, 62% play) marks it as a fine role-player, not a priority: the two toughness dies to everything. Fills a curve slot in green.
Dundoolin Weaver: Excellent value two-drop — in any creature deck (three-plus bodies) it rebuys a permanent from the graveyard on ETB. 56.1% GIH at 88% play and a 3.5 ALSA make it a quiet workhorse that turns dead lands into card advantage. Strong early pick in go-wide green.
Formidable Speaker: Premium green rare. Discard-to-tutor any creature (find your bomb or fixing) on a resilient 2/4 elf, with an untap ability for mana/combat shenanigans. 57.6% GIH across the board and 86% play — a consistent value engine, near-auto-include in green.
Gilt-Leaf's Embrace: Flash trick / protection aura. Instant-speed indestructible + trample + pump saves a creature from removal or blows out combat, and it sticks +2/+0 afterward. But at 43.8% play rate and +0.4 IWD it's card disadvantage risk — a fine role-player in a creature-heavy green deck, not a high pick.
Great Forest Druid: The best Vivid enabler among mana dorks — a 0/4 that fixes any color, blocks all day, and wears blight counters gorgeously at four toughness. LoL's "Birds of Paradise for vivid decks" nails it; solves the late-game dead-dork problem. Prioritize it in Vivid/ramp shells.
Luminollusk: Vivid role-player — a 2/4 deathtouch that gains life scaling with your colors, a fine blocker/anti-aggro brick in a multicolor base. 51.1% WR, 41% play; the deathtouch body is the real draw, the lifegain is upside. Playable in Vivid decks that stall, filler otherwise — don't overrate the ETB.
Lys Alana Dignitary: Good BG Elves two-drop. A 2/3 that behold-taxes down and later ramps GG once an Elf hits your yard — a sticky body that enables your elf top-end, and the 58.9% opening-hand WR shows it pulls early weight. Solid in the S-tier elf lane, unremarkable outside it.
Lys Alana Informant: Efficient BG Elf two-drop — a 3/1 that surveils on both entry and death, so it fuels the graveyard-as-resource plan and trades up cheaply. 57% GIH, 84% play rate: a smooth, always-fine early body in the S-tier Elves lane. Solid role-player, higher in dedicated graveyard builds.
Midnight Tilling: Excellent Elf-only enabler: mill four and return a permanent digs to your payoffs while stocking the BG graveyard, a "Malevolent Rumble variant." The flat +0.4 IWD is deceptive — its value is conditional on the Elf/graveyard shell where it's a high pick. Marginal outside BG.
Mistmeadow Council: The top green common at retro — a near-unconditional draw-a-card 4/3 that costs just {3}{G} with any Kithkin or Changeling. 56.6% GIH and 71% play; "Assault Road Pack Beast." Great in essentially any green deck. Prioritize it as your curve-filler payoff.
Moon-Vigil Adherents: Elves powerhouse. Counts creatures on board AND in the graveyard, so in a grindy BG elf deck it's an enormous, near-unkillable threat. 58.6% GIH and 89% play back LoL's "annoying enough that I need to draft it too" — a top uncommon in the S-tier pair.
Morcant's Eyes: Elves (BG) build-around bomb-uncommon. Surveils to stock the yard, then floods X 2/2 elves — and crucially counts itself when it dies, so it's never zero. LoL calls it Elves' best non-rare and a P1P1 in the right draft; 60.4% GIH, +4.4 IWD. Provides the inevitability BG craves. Prioritize when green.
Mutable Explorer: Quiet overperformer and a fine early pick — a changeling that satisfies every typal payoff, counts Vivid pips, and leaves behind a Mutavault for late-game mana or a spare body. The 2.6 ALSA (drafted early) shows the market agrees; flexible glue for any deck that wants creature types.
Pitiless Fists: LoL: "both loved it" — a fight effect stapled to a permanent +2/+2, so it's removal that also grows a threat, two-for-one at {3}{G}. 58.5% GIH WR, 88% play; the aura risk (2-for-1 if they respond) is real but the immediate fight usually resolves value. Premium green removal, high pick.
Prismabasher: Best reliably-late Vivid payoff — Ethan compares it to Mox Opal, and LoL calls it an insurance policy in any color. A 6/6 trample that pumps your team by your color count on entry; 56.5% GIH is the base rate, but it snowballs in multicolor/Vivid and wheels, so grab it as your 2c-Vivid finisher.
Prismatic Undercurrents: Trap — LoL is blunt: "if you need this, your deck probably isn't good." It only fixes/ramps five-color piles, which are bad, and true two-color Vivid doesn't want it. The 49% GIH / 45% OH / 22% play rate confirm. Leave it in the pack.
Pummeler for Hire: Textbook trap-body — beautiful stats on paper (4/4 vigilance reach ward for five, gain ~4 life) but LoL's verdict was "I wish it had a home": it doesn't affect the board enough late. 55.6% GIH with a soft OH WR. Fine filler in a Giants/ramp deck, not a payoff.
Safewright Cavalry: Clean green common — a 4/4 for four that's effectively unblockable against most boards (can't be gang-blocked) plus a mana-sink Elf pump. 56.2% GIH and 74% play make it a reliable beater and BG-elf finisher. Solid mid-pick body.
Sapling Nursery: Powerful GW/green ramp payoff. Affinity for Forests can drop it early, and each landfall makes a 3/4 reacher that snowballs the board, with an indestructible protection button. 56.4% GIH, +4.6 IWD; a strong build-around engine when your deck runs enough Forests.
Selfless Safewright: Strong flash convoke rare. A 4/2 you can flash out cheaply that grants a chosen type hexproof + indestructible is a two-for-one blowout against sweepers and removal, protecting your key typal board. 56.4% GIH, +3.0 IWD, ALSA 2.3; a flexible, high pick in any creature deck, best in tribal.
Shimmerwilds Growth: Critical Vivid enabler, not a standalone card — enchant a land to add a free off-color pip that can't be interacted with, handing you two Vivid colors. LoL calls it a green permanent plus your least-likely Vivid color. Only draft it if you're committed to Vivid; a 50% blank otherwise.
Spry and Mighty: Green combat/draw payoff — pick two of your creatures, draw and pump by their power difference. 53.6% WR, 79% play; wants a lopsided board (one big, one small) to draw multiples, otherwise it's a modest trample pump. Solid in creature-wide green decks, a fine playable that rewards board development.
Surly Farrier: Marginal two-drop. A 2/2 that sorcery-speed pumps and gives vigilance is too slow for a format that starts on three, and the negative -1.0 IWD plus 6.1 ALSA confirm it's replaceable filler. Playable only in go-wide Kithkin where the +1/+1 helps push; otherwise a sideboard body.
Tend the Sprigs: Underappreciated green ramp — LoL notes when it's "ramp into a 3/4 reach" it's genuinely good, and changelings count toward the Treefolk threshold. The soft 50% GIH and 45% OH reflect it being clunky when it whiffs the token; a fine role-player in slower green decks, replaceable in aggressive ones.
Thoughtweft Charge: Combat trick with card-draw upside if you deployed a creature that turn — +3/+3 wins fights and can replace itself. Middling numbers (54.2% GIH, +0.2 IWD) because the draw is conditional and tricks are hard to read live. A fine playable in go-wide green/Kithkin, not a priority.
Trystan, Callous Cultivator: Premium BG elf rare — a 3/4 deathtouch that mills and gains life, then flips to drain opponents by exiling Elves. 60.6% GIH, +6.3 IWD, pick-2.5 ALSA: great blocker, graveyard engine, and inevitability rolled into one. High pick that anchors BG.
Unforgiving Aim: Situational flex removal. Modal answer to flyers or enchantments, with a 2/2 elf token as the fallback when neither target exists — but the -0.9 IWD and 21% play rate show the fight-less removal is too conditional. Sideboard/reactive slot, not a maindeck pick.
Vinebred Brawler: Aggressive Elves (BG) uncommon. A 4/2 lure that forces a block and pumps another Elf +2/+1 on attack pushes damage and enables trades — a solid beater in the tribe. 55.9% GIH, +0.7 IWD reflect a synergy body that needs Elves around it; good mid pick when green, unexciting standalone.
Virulent Emissary: Excellent one-drop for BG Elves — deathtouch trades up or gums the board all game, and the go-wide lifegain trigger adds up in a token deck. 58.3% GIH with 88% play is a strong number for a one-mana body; an early-pick glue card that scales with your creature count.
Wildvine Pummeler: Vivid finisher — a 6/5 reach-trample that costs {1} less per color you control, so it lands cheap and early in a 3-4 color deck. 51.9% WR, 48% play, +2.8 IWD: the number is diluted by decks that can't discount it. Good top-end in Vivid, overcosted brick in a two-color deck — a build-around body.
Abigale, Eloquent First-Year: Excellent BW bomb — a 2-mana flying, first-strike, lifelink body that also nukes a creature's abilities and hands out its keywords, and LoL notes it pairs beautifully with Reaping Willow. The 92.9% play rate and +5.2 IWD mark it a slam-dunk two-drop in the blight guild. First-pick it.
Ashling's Command: Bomb — the best UR Elemental payoff. Choose-two flexibility means it's always a two-for-one: sweep the board for 2, draw two, copy your best Elemental, or ramp with Treasure. 66% GIH and a monster +14.8 IWD. First-pick that pulls you into UR; take it over almost anything.
Boggart Cursecrafter: The RB Goblin signpost: deathtouch 2/3 trades up all day and drains the opponent every time a Goblin dies, turning the grindy Goblin sac plan into reach. 57% GIH and +4.9 IWD confirm it's a real payoff. High pick when you're in the Goblin lane.
Bre of Clan Stoutarm: RW value engine — a 4/4 that grants flying + lifelink to your attacker and, once you've gained life, dig-and-free-casts off the top each end step. 55.8% GIH with +6.4 IWD shows the card advantage compounds. Strong Boros rare; feed it lifegain.
Brigid's Command: Premium GW gold rare. Choose-two Kithkin command that pumps, doubles, fights, or tokens — always relevant, always two-for-one value. 59.8% GIH and +6.4 IWD make it a top pick for the Kithkin pair; flexible enough to overperform even in a mediocre GW deck.
Catharsis: Flexible mythic evoke Incarnation, best in WR/aggro. The 3/4 is modal — {W}{W} makes two Kithkin, {R}{R} gives haste+anthem — and evoke lets you buy just the ETB. But the 49.9% OH WR and 53.1% GIH say it's more good-not-great here; the low ALSA (2.1) is name recognition. A strong playable, not a slam bomb.
Chaos Spewer: A 5/4 for three that's underwhelming because the drawback bites — pay 2 or blight your own board, and neither line is great without a blight payoff to soak the counters. Sub-51% GIH, negative IWD, 39.6% play mark it as a marginal RB body, not a beater you want.
Chitinous Graspling: Vanilla-ish changeling — a 3/4 reach for four that satisfies every typal payoff and blocks fliers, keeping you open in UG/tribal. 51.0% WR, 46% play; unexciting stats but changelings are format glue and this one has real defensive stats. Playable filler that gains value in a synergy deck, marginal otherwise.
Deceit: Flexible mythic in UB. A 5/5 for six that either bounces a permanent (UU) or strips their best card (BB), with an Evoke escape hatch for value even when you can't hold the body — 58.9% GIH, 87% play rate, curves late as a two-in-one. A premium UB pick; the mono-hybrid flexibility keeps you open.
Deepchannel Duelist: The premier UW Merfolk signpost — a two-mana lord that pumps the tribe AND untaps a Merfolk each end step for repeated tap-payoff and defense. LoL calls it the best Merfolk payoff that juices the whole deck fast; 63% GIH / +8.9 IWD back it. High pick that commits you to Merfolk.
Deepway Navigator: Strong UW Merfolk enabler at two mana with flash: untapping your Merfolk enables pseudo-vigilance and a wide-attack anthem. 56.3% GIH and 74.5% play are good, though it's a build-around 2/2 that needs bodies — nothing without a board. Solid tempo pickup in Merfolk.
Doran, Besieged by Time: "Most powerful card Marco had seen" — a 0/5 that discounts high-toughness creatures and turns every big-butt into a huge attacker/blocker. 58.5% GIH and a massive +10.9 IWD; ECL is full of 4-5 toughness bodies to abuse. Splash-worthy WBG bomb, take as insurance.
Dream Harvest: Clunky UB rare, mostly a trap. Seven mana to steal ~5 MV of the opponent's deck for one turn — a big swing when it lands, but the 45.6% OH and 50.3% GIH mark it as a slow, whiff-prone top-end. Playable only as a curve-topper in grindy control, not a priority.
Eclipsed Boggart: Excellent RB card-selection body. A 2/3 for three hybrid pips that digs four deep for a Goblin/land keeps your grindy deck fueled and fixes early — 58.9% GIH, +6.2 IWD. Castable in mono-B or mono-R too. A consistent, high-floor early pick in the Goblin lane.
Eclipsed Elf: A premium BG Elf engine and high pick — a 3/2 for three that digs four deep for an Elf, Swamp, or Forest is card advantage plus a body plus fixing. The gold-pip flexibility casts it on turn two, and the numbers are elite: 63% GIH, +8.1 IWD, 83% play. Slam in BG.
Eclipsed Flamekin: Excellent UR common-quality engine (uncommon) — a 1/4 that digs four deep for an Elemental, Island, or Mountain, smoothing draws and finding payoffs. 59.9% GIH WR, +6.7 IWD, 82% play; the wall body blocks early aggro while the ETB fixes and finds gas. High pick in UR Elementals, strong wherever you're U/R.
Eclipsed Kithkin: Best of the Eclipsed cycle, per LoL — a two-mana 2/1 whose top-four dig finds lands (huge on turn two), Kithkin, changelings, or Nameless Inversion. The 64.5% opening-hand WR and +7.7 IWD reflect that smoothing; a high pick in GW and strong anywhere the hybrid fits.
Eclipsed Merrow: Excellent UW Merfolk uncommon — a 2/3 for three hybrid pips that digs four deep for a Merfolk, Plains, or Island, so it's a body plus card selection that fixes and finds threats. 62% GIH / +6.8 IWD, castable in mono-W or mono-U. Reliable high playable in the tribe.
Emptiness: Flexible mythic that's always live — evoke or hard-cast, and the mode you pay for (reanimate a 3-drop with WW, or -3/-3 removal with BB) fits BW perfectly. ALSA 1.6 and +5.6 IWD confirm first-pick status; the split modes mean it's never a dead card. Bomb.
Feisty Spikeling: Changeling that keeps your tribal options open while providing a 2/1 first-striker on offense — but a fragile body drags the numbers (50.7% GIH, negative IWD). Value it as an enabler that satisfies every typal payoff and Vivid pips, not as a good creature. Flexible filler.
Figure of Fable: Bomb, and the chunk's best card. A one-mana hybrid leveler that becomes a 7/8 with protection from your opponents — an uncontested mana sink that wins games solo. 63.6% GIH, +10.6 IWD, 1.6 ALSA, 94% play: first-pick, splashable, take it every time.
Flaring Cinder: Key Elementals (UR) engine and Vivid filter. A 3/2 for three that loots on ETB and on each MV-4+ spell smooths draws and fixes, plus the relevant Elemental type. 55.2% GIH; the value scales with a top-heavy curve. Solid pick in UR, fine in Vivid — take it when you're filtering.
Gangly Stompling: A clean aggressive changeling body — 4/2 trample for three with every creature type is great curve filler that enables typal payoffs and pressures early. Average WR (53.7%) because the 2 toughness dies easily, but the flexibility and playability make it a solid RG/aggro role-player.
Glister Bairn: Vivid combat payoff — a 1/4 that pumps another creature by your color count each combat, a repeatable evasion/trample enabler in multicolor decks. 52.3% WR, 52% play; the number depends on hitting 3+ colors and having a threat to pump. Good engine in Vivid/UG, mediocre in a two-color shell — its {2}{G/U}{G/U}{G/U} cost also demands commitment.
Grub's Command: Powerful RB Goblins payoff — a modal Command that copies a Goblin, pumps/hastes your team, kills a creature/artifact, and refills off a Goblin mill, any two per cast. 62.7% GIH and +11.8 IWD; the removal-plus-value flexibility makes it a top uncommon-slot pick, best when you're deep in Goblins.
High Perfect Morcant: Bomb rare for BG Elves — every Elf ETB makes each opponent blight a creature, so it grinds their board while your own elves flood in, plus a proliferate sink to snowball counters. 4/4 for four, 62% GIH / +9.1 IWD. First-pick that anchors the S-tier Elves deck.
Hovel Hurler: Big hybrid Giant with a slow evasion engine — a 6/7 for five (after counters) that grants flying to your team by shedding counters. Middling 53.1% GIH and a weak 49.3% OH WR flag it as clunky early, but the RW beatdown ceiling is real. Playable role-player, not a bomb.
Kirol, Attentive First-Year: "Most fun rare in the set," a 3/3 that copies your triggered abilities (Luminal Holds, goblin death-triggers, Kithkeeper) by tapping two creatures. But 52.7% GIH says it's a build-around, not a slam — you need a dense trigger package to pay off. Medium Boros pick.
Lluwen, Imperfect Naturalist: Strong BG rare. ETB self-mill sets up the graveyard-as-resource plan and fixes your draw, while the Worm-token activation is a real mana sink and finisher. 58.8% GIH and 2.3 ALSA — a top pick in S-tier BG elves, resilient and grindy.
Maralen, Fae Ascendant: Bomb in Elves/Fairies (UBG). A 4/5 flyer that exiles opponent cards on every Elf/Faerie ETB and lets you free-cast from them snowballs fast in the right shell — 60.4% GIH, a huge +10.3 IWD. Three colors is the only cost; when you're in this lane it's a first-pick engine that also blocks and flies.
Merrow Skyswimmer: A UW workhorse that rose all format — convoke lets you flash it out cheaply for a 2/2 flying vigilance plus a token, enabling huge tempo turns. LoL stopped thinking of it as Merfolk-only: "just good in blue or white." 57% GIH, 81% play; take it early in UW.
Mischievous Sneakling: LoL's confirmed best common changeling — a 2/2 flash that ambushes attackers ("never attack into two open mana in Dimir") and fills blue+black pips for Vivid while satisfying every tribe. 52.4% WR undersells it; the flash body plus universal synergy is why it's 75% played. High-value common, snap it in UB/flash and take it to stay open anywhere.
Morcant's Loyalist: The BG Elf lord signpost — a 3/2 that pumps other Elves and recurs one from your yard on death, looping with a second copy per LoL. 61.3% GIH, +6.8 IWD, curves at three; a high pick that anchors the S-tier elves lane. Take it as your BG commitment card.
Noggle Robber: Essential Vivid glue — a 3/3 for three that counts as two colors and throws off two Treasures across entry and death, letting you spike off-color payoffs early. LoL calls it "essential" in Vivid; 57% GIH / +4.6 IWD and 82% play rate. High pick whenever you're in the Vivid/Temur base.
Prideful Feastling: The glue card — a 2/3 lifelink changeling that stabilizes, counts for every typal payoff, and reads as two colors for Vivid. Golden Egg winner for archetype flexibility; 52.9% GIH looks plain but its value is being splashable everywhere. High pick to keep your deck open.
Raiding Schemes: Five-mana conspire enchantment that copies your noncreature spells — a build-around that needs both a critical mass of spells and spare creatures to tap. Null WR off 2.4% play means almost nobody made it work. Trap; leave it unless your RG deck is spell-loaded.
Reaping Willow: Premier BW blight payoff — LoL's "number one in my heart." A 3/6 lifelink for four (effectively 1/4 immediately) that reanimates cheap creatures once you shed the counters via blight removal. 56.9% GIH and +5.0 IWD; a high pick that anchors the blight deck.
Sanar, Innovative First-Year: Vivid bomb. At 92.6% play rate and +8.0 IWD, this 2/4 is a repeatable free-cast engine that scales with your color count — exactly the Vivid payoff the format overrates on WR, but here the number is earned and the body blocks well. Slam it in any multicolor/Vivid deck; near-P1P1.
Shadow Urchin: A grindy RB blight rare that generates real card advantage — attack to blight, then cash dying counter-creatures into impulse-drawn cards. The 3/4 body survives, and it snowballs in a deck built to kill its own creatures. 53.7% GIH undersells the engine ceiling; strong in RB/BW blight.
Stoic Grove-Guide: BG grind creature — a 5/4 for five that leaves an Elf token behind via graveyard activation, decent value in an attrition deck. But -3.1 IWD and a middling 52.6% WR flag it: the 5/4 dies to everything and the recursion is slow. Playable body in BG Elves, but don't overvalue — it's a filler beater with upside.
Sygg's Command: Solid UW Merfolk Command. Two of: copy a Merfolk, team lifelink, draw, or tap-and-stun — the tap-down plus card draw gives it a floor even without a wide merfolk board. 58.7% GIH and +5.2 IWD; a reliable value pick that rewards the tempo/convoke UW lane.
Tam, Mindful First-Year: Protective UG glue rare — a 1/2 for two that gives your other creatures hexproof-from-their-colors, blanking a lot of targeted removal, plus a make-all-colors ability that turns on Vivid pips. The 53% GIH / 93% play rate split shows near-universal inclusion but modest impact; solid early pick, protection more than power.
Thoughtweft Lieutenant: GW Kithkin payoff: every Kithkin ETB pumps and tramples a creature, snowballing into a freight train. 58.8% GIH and +4.3 IWD are strong, but LoL flags the whole Kithkin plan folds to one removal spell. High pick in the tribe, but hold your own removal for the mirror.
Trystan's Command: BG elves bomb — a modal command that copies an Elf, rebuys two cards, kills a creature/enchantment, or blows out combat, choosing two. 63.7% GIH and +11.3 IWD (66% drawn WR) make it one of the best cards in the pair. First-pick in BG.
Twinflame Travelers: Strong UR gold uncommon. A 3/3 flyer that doubles every Elemental trigger — turns your ETB midrange plan into overwhelming value. 57.2% GIH and +4.9 IWD confirm it overdelivers; a priority pick that's still a solid evasive body without the synergy.
Vibrance: Bomb, near-unconditional. A 4/4 for five with modal evoke — {R}{R} deals 3 to any target, {G}{G} ramps/fixes and gains life — that's efficient removal, a body, or both. 61.5% GIH, +10.0 IWD, ALSA 1.7. Flexible, always live, splashable via hybrid. A top-pick anywhere in RG/Temur.
Voracious Tome-Skimmer: The UB Fairies/flash payoff — a 2/3 flyer that turns every opponent's-turn spell into a card, drawing you deep in a dedicated flash shell. LoL: "a really excellent payoff for the deck." The 36% play and modest raw WR show that number is conditioned on UB; a build-around, not a splash.
Wary Farmer: LoL grew to love it — a 3/3 for three that surveils each turn you develop your board, keeping gas flowing and enabling graveyard synergies in any G/W deck. 54.8% WR, flat across OH/GD (consistent), 68% play. Unflashy but a well-sized body with card selection; solid role-player that fits Kithkin, Elves, and Vivid alike.
Wistfulness: Flexible UG mythic bomb — a 6/5 for five that exiles an artifact/enchantment (GG) or loots for two (UU), with Evoke to bank the ETB when you need the mode more than the body. Elite 92.4% play rate, +9.5 IWD, 1.6 ALSA; the hybrid cost keeps it splashable. First-pick material.
Chronicle of Victory: Bomb tribal payoff — a 6-mana artifact that anthems your chosen type +2/+2 with first strike and trample AND draws a card off every spell of that type. 62% GIH, +9.7 IWD, 1.2 ALSA, 98% play rate — near-universally slammed and it runs away with games. First-pick.
Dawn-Blessed Pennant: "Already-good-get-gooder" glue: cheap tribal payoff that trickles life and recurs a key creature from the yard. 53.8% GIH and a negative IWD show it does little on its own — it juices decks that are already synergy-rich. A fine cheap include in committed tribal decks, filler elsewhere.
Firdoch Core: Colorless fixing that ramps and, as a Changeling, counts for every tribe and adds any color — plus it can swing as a 4/4 in a pinch. 50.8% GIH and 28% play peg it as a Vivid/multicolor role-player; skip it in a clean two-color deck. Niche fixing.
Foraging Wickermaw: Vivid enabler. A 1/3 that surveils on entry and fixes/adds a color each turn — the glue that turns on off-color payoffs in Vivid light-splash builds. 53.6% GIH; LoL rates it well for Vivid but weak in strict two-color. Draft it as an engine piece, not a beater.
Gathering Stone: Powerful but only if a tribal lane is open. {1}-off your chosen type plus repeatable card advantage widens the gap for already-strong typal decks — LoL half-hates that it exists. 58.3% GIH is the committed-tribal number; a high pick when your tribe is flowing, a dead card in a scattershot deck.
Mirrormind Crown: Trap. A four-mana equipment whose token-copy payoff requires you to already be making tokens AND have a creature worth copying — far too many moving parts. 39.4% GIH, -7.4 IWD, 5.2% play make it one of the worst cards in the set. Do not play.
Puca's Eye: LoL: "plus one vivid for free, and it cantrips" — a 2-mana artifact that draws on ETB, counts as a color for Vivid, and turns into a card-draw engine once you hit five colors. 24% play rate is because only Vivid decks want it, but +5.0 IWD and 54.6% WR show it wins the late game there. Auto-include in Vivid, unplayable elsewhere — pure build-around.
Springleaf Drum: Niche mana rock — LoL flags it as only situationally useful in Vivid decks for fixing your off-color payoffs. Exactly 50% GIH and a 24.6% play rate say it's a marginal, deck-specific include; skip it unless you're base-Vivid and need to hit multiple colors reliably.
Stalactite Dagger: Trap equipment — LoL gives it "two thumbs down" because it doesn't auto-equip, so you get a 2-mana 1/1 changeling token plus an equip you rarely pay for. 51% GIH / -0.7 IWD / 22% play rate confirm it didn't matter. The changeling token has minor typal use; otherwise skip.
Blood Crypt: Fixing for RB/Goblins — untapped for 2 life or tapped otherwise. 52.4% GIH is baseline land value, but the fixing smooths a two-color aggressive base and enables splashes. Take it around mid-pack when in the Rakdos colors; a luxury, not a payoff.
Eclipsed Realms: The set's fixing land — choose a tribe on entry and it taps for any color for that type. LoL: normally you'd never play these, but they work here for multicolor and Vivid builds. 53.7% GIH and 68% play. Fine glue for greedy manabases, not a priority pick.
Evolving Wilds: Fixing staple for Vivid and splash decks. Fetches a basic tapped to smooth mana and turn on color-count payoffs — LoL calls it excellent Vivid fixing. 94% play rate; take it whenever you're greedy on colors, otherwise a fine mana-consistency include.
Hallowed Fountain: Solid dual land for UW. Untapped-for-2-life fixing is a real bonus in a tempo deck that wants to curve out. The 52.9% GIH is fine for a land; take it when you're in Merfolk/UW and want the mana consistency, but don't over-prioritize a land over playables.
Overgrown Tomb: A premium BG shock land — untapped fixing for two life smooths any two-color base and enables splashes. Fixing WR always reads flat (54.2%, +0.0 IWD) because it wins by being in your deck, not drawn; take it highly in any B/G deck, especially the S-tier Elves pair.
Steam Vents: Untapped-for-2-life UR dual — perfect fixing for Elementals/Izzet and any deck splashing U or R. 53.1% WR, flat 0.0 IWD (lands don't swing games directly), 62% play. The fixing is the value; take it reasonably early in two/three-color UR builds, it enables your splashes and Vivid counts.
Temple Garden: Playable dual land for GW decks — untapped for 2 life or tapped, standard fixing with a Forest/Plains typeline (relevant for Eclipsed Kithkin's dig). The slightly negative IWD is normal for a land; take it as fixing when you're in green-white, not as a spell slot.
Idyllic Tutor: Enchantment tutor with no real Limited home — 5% play rate and null WR mean drafters correctly leave it in the pack. There's no enchantment worth building a tutor around in ECL; the read is provisional on missing data, but this is a sideboard/cut card at best.
Kinsbaile Cavalier: Data-blind rare (no WR filed), but the ALSA of 4.0 and 53.8% play say the field respected it — a Kithkin Knight that historically doubled attack triggers. Provisional read: a solid GW Kithkin build-around that rewards a go-wide board, worth an early speculative pick in the tribe.
Mistbind Clique: No ECL data (null WR, but a 3.4 ALSA and 49% play show it gets taken and run). The classic Lorwyn flash 4/4 flyer that taps the opponent out of a land untap is a proven tempo blowout — provisional strong pick in UB/UW faeries, read is stat-light.
Wanderwine Prophets: No WR data — provisional read. A merfolk champion payoff whose ceiling (extra turns via champion sac) is a build-around that rarely comes together in Limited. 45% play rate suggests most drafters can't reliably enable it; treat as a niche UW merfolk gamble, not a reliable pick.
Bitterblossom: Faerie enchantment that drips a 1/1 flyer each turn at the cost of life — an evasive token engine and a build-around for UB Fairies. The +8.3 IWD and 1.7 ALSA show it's picked and powerful in the token/Fairy shell, though the pinging life and no immediate board make it deck-dependent. High pick in Fairies.
Faerie Macabre: Sideboard/niche graveyard hate — a pitchable Faerie that exiles from yards for free, relevant only against recursion-heavy BG/UB decks. 6.5% play says it's rarely maindecked in Limited; a body you board in, not a card you draft to play.
Goblin Chieftain: Goblin lord rare — +1/+1 and haste to your Goblins, an aggressive anchor that turns a wide RB board into immediate damage. 56.9% GIH WR and a big +7.3 IWD reflect the lord multiplier, but that number is conditioned on a real Goblin board. Bomb in RB Goblins, mediocre off-tribe; prioritize it if you're in the lane.
Goblin Sharpshooter: Sleeper rare that Numot respects as a near-game-winner — it pings for 1 whenever any creature dies and untaps with each death, going nuclear alongside deathtouch or a token-death engine. The 60.7% GIH and +10.8 IWD confirm the power; a high pick in RB Goblins where deaths are constant.
Heat Shimmer: Provisional read on null data — a red copy/clone-flavored rare with only 16.8% play rate, so most drafters cut it. Situational at best in this grindy format; treat as a marginal late playable pending real numbers, not a priority pick.
Devoted Druid: Elf mana-dork role-player: 51.8% GIH and +0.6 IWD are modest, but 79.6% play means it's a near-default Elf/ramp two-drop for accelerating into your payoffs. Fragile 0/2-style body invites removal, so it's an enabler, not a threat. Fine early pick in BG/Vivid.
Helix Pinnacle: Build-around enchantment win-con with no Limited application in ECL — 0.2% play and null WR confirm it never sees a deck. Provisional, but the read is clear: skip it entirely.
Leaf-Crowned Visionary: Strong green rare. An elf lord that anthems your tribe and draws a card whenever you cast an elf — exactly the card-advantage engine BG elves wants. 59.2% GIH, +5.0 IWD, 2.5 ALSA; a high pick that both pumps the board and refills your hand.
Regal Force: Big green Elemental payoff, but underwhelming here — 51.5% GIH and -0.6 IWD say it's not carrying games despite the rare tag and low ALSA. A top-end body that needs a wide board to draw well and does nothing the turn it lands; a fine curve-topper in a creature-heavy green deck, not a bomb.
Manamorphose: A free color-fixing cantrip that's essentially deck lubricant — replaces itself while fixing your mana, most useful in a greedy Vivid/multicolor RG base. 47.7% play with no WR data; a fine filler that never costs you a card, but adds no board presence.
Risen Reef: Elite Elemental engine — every Elemental ETB (including its own) ramps a land and draws, snowballing UR/UG Elementals out of reach. Best numbers in the chunk: 62.2% GIH WR, +10.1 IWD, 74% play. This is the payoff the archetype is built around; a bomb in Elementals, take it very early and let it define your deck.
Slippery Bogle: Data-thin (11.2% play rate, no WR) — a hexproof beater that only matters as an aura target, and ECL has few auras worth suiting up. Provisional read: a fringe UG playable at best, effectively a sideboard body. Leave it unless you've built an aggressive aura shell.
Dolmen Gate: Colorless artifact with a healthy 60% play rate and a low 3.2 ALSA despite null WR — drafters are taking and running it early, suggesting a real go-wide/aggro enabler (protecting attackers). Provisional on missing WR, but the pick and play data point to a solid, splashable role-player.
Door of Destinies: Tribal snowball artifact — grows every time you cast a creature of the chosen type, a build-around that gets out of hand in a dense tribal deck. ALSA 2.0 and 84.7% play with +3.7 IWD show the field slams it, but it's a do-nothing on an empty board. High pick only when committed to a tribe.
Painter's Servant: Colorless Scarecrow with no ECL stats to lean on (19% play, null WR). Its color-fixing/naming ability is a combo tool with little Limited upside here — provisional, but treat it as a niche curiosity rather than a maindeck card absent a specific synergy.
Thousand-Year Elixir: Unplayable in Limited. A 1.4% play rate and no meaningful WR data confirm the untap-artifact does nothing without a strong tap-ability base to abuse. Leave it in the pack; it's effectively a blank in this format.
